key_insight: A single, transferable machine‑learning model can predict spin–orbit–coupled electronic structure across the periodic table, enabling fast, accurate exploration of relativistic quantum materials.
problem_solved: Accurately modeling spin–orbit coupling (SOC) with quantum calculations is computationally expensive and hard to generalize across chemistries, which blocks high‑throughput discovery of SOC‑driven quantum materials and devices.
method: Develop a universal ML framework trained on SOC‑inclusive electronic‑structure reference data spanning many elements and compounds.
Incorporate physics‑aware inductive biases (symmetry/relativistic sensitivity and element dependence) so the model generalizes across the periodic table.
Use the model to directly predict SOC‑coupled electronic properties (e.g., band structures, splittings) for rapid high‑throughput screening.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a pretrained, SOC‑aware modeling paradigm that brings relativistic electronic effects into scalable workflows, enabling transfer learning and orders‑of‑magnitude faster materials screening compared with ab initio methods.
visual_elements: Schematic of the ML workflow: inputs (structure, element) → SOC‑aware model → predicted SOC‑coupled band structure/properties

paper_title: Towards a universal model for spin–orbit physics
paper_authors: Atul C. Thakur, Shyue Ping Ong
